newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Opel to maintain sick pay pact.
newsitem.headline: German Opel to maintain sick pay pact.

text.p: General Motor Co's German unit Adam Opel AG said on Wednesday it would maintain an earlier agreement with workers not to enforce sick pay cuts until contractual or legal agreement had been reached on the matter.

Opel issued the statement following the collapse of talks on sick pay and other wage issues between the IG Metall trade union and the Gestamtmetall engineering employers federation early on Wednesday morning.

But the car-maker said that, in accordance with the original agreement it had reached with its workers council, it would continue to document sick days taken by employees in case the sick pay measures were to be applied retrospectively.
A new law came into effect at the start of this month allowing employers to cut sick payments to 80 percent of salary from the current 100 percent.
Unions have protested that the cuts went against specific clauses guaranteeing full sick pay in the wage contracts of many of their members.
Other employers in the sector such as Daimler-Benz were forced to postpone plans to implement the cuts immediately after workers organised mass protests across the industry.
